name: Proxmox VE
description: Core metrics for Proxmox VE, grouped like with like: cluster health and capacity, then CPU, memory, storage and network, then top-10 tables of guests, nodes and storage, guest state and alerts.

config.name: Cluster Health
config.description: Health Score is nodes online weighted by how stalled each one is (pressure stall figures), 0 without quorum; 100 is every node online and unstalled. It warns below 70 and errors below 50.

config.name: Capacity and Overcommit
config.description: Overcommit is allocated over physical capacity across the cluster. The ratios ship without thresholds; a defensible number is site-specific.

config.name: Cluster Health Over Time
config.description: Only the resource collecting for the cluster draws a line; the standby's stays empty unless it stood in.

config.name: Node Load Per Core
config.description: Load average normalised by core count, which is the form that compares across differently sized nodes.

config.name: Node CPU Pressure
config.description: Share of time some task waited for CPU (pressure stall information): contention that utilisation alone does not show.

config.name: Node Memory Pressure
config.description: Share of time some task waited for memory: reclaim and swap stalls before memory runs out.

config.name: Node IO Pressure
config.description: IO pressure is the share of time some task waited for IO; IO wait is CPU time spent idle with IO outstanding.

config.name: Guest Disk Throughput
config.description: Byte counters only. Proxmox exposes no per-guest IOPS or storage latency, so there is no equivalent of the Nutanix latency graphs.

config.name: Guest Network Throughput
config.description: netin/netout are cumulative counters in Proxmox and are collected as derive, so this is a rate rather than a climbing total.
Containers only: Proxmox reports disk use for containers but not for VMs, so VMs have no row here.
config.name: Top 10 Guests by Disk Used

config.description: Status ships without a threshold: a stopped guest is usually stopped on purpose. HAError only fires for guests the cluster itself considers broken.
config.name: Guest Status
